title: What to Measure Next: Leading Indicators and Promises Versus Proof

web_blocks.text: RNIT’s next stage should be judged through observable indicators, not a catalogue of aspirations. FY2026 revenue and PAT grew over the first post-relisting operating year, while H1 FY2027 showed higher revenue and PAT but negative operating cash flow, larger receivables and reduced cash. That makes cash conversion at least as important as sales growth. Distinguish audited annual figures, limited-review interim data, management usage claims and future intentions; they answer different questions and should not be merged into one confidence score. [1] [2] [3]

web_blocks.text: First, measure revenue quality, not just revenue growth. FY2026 operating revenue increased about 60% over FY2025 and PAT about 67%, but FY2025 was the first year including the merged operating business. Growth is useful but early. The audited segment combines AI, software, consulting and support. Domestic services were ₹3,382.43 lakh and exports ₹1,767.45 lakh in FY2026, but customer identities and concentration are not reported. Ask for recurring versus project revenue, renewal rates and reconciliation of management’s SaaS description to audited sales. [1] [2]

Second, measure cash quality. FY2026 CFO was ₹1,123.15 lakh, but capex and intangible purchases were ₹1,896.75 lakh. CFO includes positive borrowing and tax-liability adjustments, while receivables and other current assets absorbed funds. H1 FY2027 posted ₹550.92 lakh PAT alongside negative ₹710.32 lakh CFO. This does not negate profitability; it demonstrates why collections must be tracked separately. Follow invoices and customer receipts, including whether advances unwind as delivery progresses. [1] [3]

Third, monitor receivable ageing and acceptance timing. At March 2026, ₹2,063.34 lakh of unsecured receivables were classified as good; ₹449.19 lakh was aged one to two years from due date, with no balance older than two years. The company reported no ECL allowance. By September, receivables had risen to ₹3,084.54 lakh. That could reflect growth or delayed milestones; public data cannot distinguish. Track later collections, disputes, unbilled contract assets and top-customer exposure. The auditor’s revenue-recognition focus makes these leading indicators particularly relevant. [1] [3]

Fourth, recurring revenue and renewal need numerical definitions. Management says SaaS and O&M supported FY2025 and the accounting policy recognizes subscriptions and managed-service contracts. Yet the filings do not provide subscription share, ARR, churn, cohort renewals or contract durations. The September 2026 APSSDC NIA award scopes up to 20 lakh users/interview sessions, but does not report completed sessions or paid minutes. [43] Follow paid active users, renewal without rebid, support load and revenue recognition by product. Until the company reports these metrics, do not treat “SaaS” as proof of a recurring-revenue engine. [1] [2] [5]

Fifth, track acceptance throughput: award-to-deployment time, deployment-to-sign-off, unbilled revenue, invoice timing and extensions. The auditor identifies stage of completion, customer acceptance and contract assets as areas requiring judgment and describes testing contracts, timesheets and confirmations. A regular record of timely acceptance would support execution quality. A persistent contract-asset or aged-receivable build would warrant scrutiny even if profit rises. RNIT has not published project-level delivery metrics, so balance-sheet proxies are imperfect until management reports better data. [1]

Sixth, measure delivery leverage. FY2026 had 76 employees, employee benefits of ₹795.29 lakh and consultancy charges of ₹1,460.27 lakh. Consultancy may be a flexible capacity choice, but it exceeded payroll. Revenue per employee alone could therefore mislead. Track consultancy content, billable work, product-development capitalization, support headcount and implementation effort. The key question is whether each additional deployment requires proportionately less engineering and integration. The current reports establish the cost mix, not the answer. [1]

Management reports more than three billion cumulative facial verifications and fifteen million daily digital interactions in FY2025 and the November 2025 update. These are potentially meaningful usage claims, but definitions and economics are absent: unique people versus repeated events, live versus historical checks, geography, error rates and revenue attribution are not reconciled. A large event count can represent throughput without proving paid frequency or contribution. Ask management for definitions and customer-level reconciliation rather than accepting or rejecting the claim in isolation. [2] [7]

Capacity and total addressable market are not evidenced in a form that supports extrapolation. RNIT reports 76 employees, aggregate export services and named project scopes, but not platform throughput, utilization, customer implementation capacity, backlog or product TAM. APSSDC’s September 2026 award scopes up to 20 lakh users/interview sessions, but that project ceiling is not enterprise-wide throughput or achieved adoption. [43] Management’s international and global-leadership aspirations are not contracted markets. Monitor accepted projects, repeat revenue, export collections and deployment effort. [1] [2] [5]

No earnings-call transcript appears in the permitted research set, so no call quotations are used. The annual-report shareholder letters are the available management record. FY2026 discusses custom language models, IP, global partnerships and products foundational to government and enterprise. These are priorities, not delivered outcomes. Track product releases, paid deployments, recurring revenue and cash returns. Quarterly, review revenue, PAT, receivables, cash and borrowings; annually, review audited mix, impairment, related parties, staffing, governance and collections. Keep interim and audited periods separate. [1] [2] [3]

Management’s scale claims need consistent definitions before becoming KPIs. Three billion verifications could include repeat checks of the same individual; fifteen million daily interactions may combine different products or event types. The annual report and November update do not publish unique-user counts, error rates, geography, uptime or revenue attribution. Ask management to reconcile activity with customer deployments and service commitments. These claims may evidence throughput, but should remain separate from audited sales, customer cash and recurring contracts. [2] [7]

Capacity and TAM are not disclosed in a form that supports precise extrapolation. RNIT reports 76 employees and several public engagements, but not platform throughput, implementation capacity, server utilization, product TAM or backlog. APSSDC’s September 2026 NIA award covers up to 20 lakh users/interview sessions, but that project scope is not general enterprise capacity or achieved usage. [43] Global expansion is an aspiration, not a contracted market. Monitor accepted projects, launch times, export collections and reuse across customers. This converts management’s ambition into measurable operating evidence without inventing market share. [1] [2] [5]

The KPI hierarchy should place audited financial measures beside delivery measures. Revenue and PAT show recognized activity; CFO and capex show cash after investment; ageing and contract assets show whether acceptance and collections keep pace. Renewal tests durability; acceptance and extensions test delivery; consultancy and headcount test scalability. No single metric is sufficient. Because one segment hides product mix, pair each aggregate figure with an explicit disclosure gap rather than treating growth as proof across all products. [1] [3]

Quarterly interim results need careful labels. H1 FY2027 revenue and PAT rose year on year, while CFO was negative and receivables expanded. The figures are unaudited and limited-reviewed. Do not compare half-year CFO directly with a full-year amount or combine it with annual income for an improvised conversion ratio. At year-end, reconcile full-year cash flow with customer receipts and investment. This safeguard prevents the most common misreading of the company’s current cash profile. [3]

A practical reporting cadence separates leading and lagging indicators. Awards and planned user counts are leading signals; accepted go-lives and recurring invoices are closer to realized business; cash receipts and impairment tests are lagging confirmation. Record the source and period beside each number. A claim from an annual letter, a BSE announcement, an audited statement and an unaudited half-year should not be scored equally. For an early company, a small dashboard can still be rigorous if it captures revenue, margins, receivables, CFO, capex, contract assets, renewals and staffing intensity and flags unknowns explicitly. [1] [2] [3] [7]

One more practical KPI is the ratio of recognized revenue to cash actually collected over a rolling annual period, reconciled to receivable movement and advances. Use audited annual figures where available and mark interim values as unaudited. This ratio would make it harder for growth in milestones awaiting acceptance to masquerade as a stable cash engine. Pair it with capex and intangible purchases so the full cash burden of scaling is visible. [1] [3]

epigraph.quote: The next era will not be defined by software alone. It will be defined by intelligent systems that continuously learn, adapt and create value.
epigraph.author: Raja Srinivas Nandigam, Managing Director’s message, FY2026 annual report [1]

book_paragraphs: Your monitoring system should be small enough to use and sharp enough to change your mind. Begin with revenue and earnings, CFO and investment, receivable ageing and contract assets, recurring share and renewal, project acceptance, and delivery intensity. The annual reports provide partial baselines but not a complete product scorecard. That matters because a young software company can report attractive bookings or earnings while collections, support burden and renewals remain unknown. The goal is to see whether sales, profit and cash begin to move together after restructuring, not to find one flattering ratio. [1] [2]

Revenue and PAT grew in FY2026, but compare them against the right baseline. FY2025 was the first post-relisting year incorporating RNIT Solutions & Services, and FY2026 was the first full year under the new name. The increase is audited, but the segment note combines software, AI, consulting and support. Sales growth does not reveal whether Faceify subscriptions grew, an implementation was accepted, or export sales came from one account. Ask for recurring and project revenue, renewals and customer concentration. Until then, treat aggregate revenue as evidence of scale-up, not proof of a product flywheel. [1] [2]

Cash conversion is the central near-term test. FY2026 CFO was positive and close to PAT, but capex and intangible purchases exceeded it. The CFO reconciliation also contains borrowing and tax-liability inflows, while receivables and current assets consumed funds. H1 FY2027 then showed positive profit alongside negative CFO. These facts do not invalidate earnings; they show that cash depends on working-capital timing and investment. Follow actual customer receipts rather than just the reported CFO line, and distinguish financing from customer-funded growth. [1] [3]

Receivable ageing offers a concrete warning system. FY2026 shows ₹449.19 lakh aged one to two years and ₹172.77 lakh six months to one year; the rest was under six months. Management classifies balances as good and records no loss allowance. That is an audited assessment, but it does not prove collection. Receivables then rose to ₹3,084.54 lakh by September 2026. Ask whether this reflects new deployments, pending sign-offs or concentrated accounts, and track subsequent cash receipts. This is more informative than a debtor-day ratio from a changing early revenue base. [1] [3]

Recurring revenue would change business quality, but it needs a numerical definition. The company says SaaS and O&M support results and recognizes subscription arrangements, but does not report recurring share, ARR, churn, renewal or duration. NIA’s planned user scope is not completed sessions or recurring fees. Ask whether subscriptions bill in advance, whether the buyer must rebid, how support is included and how much use is paid. If these disclosures remain unavailable, retain SaaS as a strategic possibility rather than an established stabilizer. [1] [2] [5]

Acceptance throughput is a leading indicator because the auditor names it as a key judgment. An award is early; deployment, milestone certification, invoice and receipt are successive proof points. Use contract assets and aged receivables as imperfect proxies, but request project-level data. Track award-to-go-live, sign-off lag and post-period cash. If these improve while sales grow, execution quality is strengthening. If not, earnings may be recognized ahead of cash. The unmodified audit opinion deserves respect; continued monitoring is not an accusation. [1] [6]

The labor mix tells you what kind of scale is being built. RNIT had 76 employees, spent ₹7.95 crore on benefits and ₹14.60 crore on consultancy. That may reflect flexible implementation capacity, but it weakens the assumption that incremental software revenue has negligible cost. Ask whether consultants are customer-billable, building common products or maintaining deployments. Track this cost alongside product-development additions and support obligations. Revenue per permanent employee alone can look unusually high if delivery is purchased outside payroll. [1]

Management’s usage and strategy claims may be important, but they need definitions. Billions of verifications do not say whether events are unique, repeated, paid, accurate or concentrated in one customer. A memorandum or project capacity does not equal collected recurring revenue. Separate deployed systems, contracted scope, active use, renewal and customer cash. This method does not dismiss ambition; it makes it testable. No earnings-call transcript is available in this permitted set, so use attributed annual-report language rather than inventing call quotations. [1] [2] [7]

Score the company quarterly but interpret it annually. A half-year can be distorted by collections or milestone timing, especially in a recently reorganized business. FY2026 is one full audited view; H1 FY2027 is an interim stress test. Keep them separate and follow up at year-end. The evidence threshold should rise with time: a real customer can validate initial delivery, but durable quality requires renewals, collections, product reuse and returns on development. If RNIT reports these, the business becomes easier to assess. If not, keep a conditional view rather than filling gaps with aspiration. [1] [3]

A useful dashboard should make it possible for you to change your mind. Revenue growth supports optimism; negative half-year CFO and higher receivables should temper it. A SaaS label may suggest recurrence; missing renewal data keeps the inference open. A government agreement establishes a buyer; acceptance and cash establish execution. By placing those evidence layers side by side, you avoid deciding in advance that every new disclosure confirms one thesis. [1] [3]

No earnings-call transcript is in the permitted set. You have annual-report letters and formal exchange announcements, not a basis to quote a call or invent management commentary. Use attributed shareholder-letter language and compare it with delivery. Global expansion, custom models and foundational platforms are priorities; releases, paid use, renewal and cash are outcomes. [1] [2]

Your KPI dashboard should preserve an explicit “not disclosed” category. That is more informative than estimating SaaS share from a CEO letter or customer concentration from a small number of named cases. A transparent unknown is a diligence item that can be resolved later; an invented proxy becomes false certainty. Pair what is known—audited revenue, PAT, CFO, capex, receivables and expenses—with a clear request for renewals, paid usage and project acceptance. Then update the judgment only when new evidence arrives. [1] [2] [3]

Management’s FY2026 letter says, “Our objective is not simply to participate in the AI revolution, but to build platforms that become foundational to how governments and enterprises operate in the years ahead.” You and I should treat that as a strategic promise, not a result. The tests are repeatable deployments, renewals, product-level contribution and customer cash. [1]

The newest commercial KPI is the APSSDC NIA award’s usage contract. It allows up to 20 lakh users or interview sessions, up to two attempts for pursuing students with a three-month gap, and one attempt for other users. The commercial basis is per minute per user, and the filed term is five years from signing. These are designed capacity and contract conditions, not observed demand. You should monitor actual sessions, minutes, completed interviews, assessment quality, unit compute cost, acceptance and cash. [43]

The same award is classified Tier 7, above ₹25 crore including GST under RNIT’s reporting policy. That indicates a large contract category, but actual billings depend on usage and satisfactory delivery. The right walk-the-talk test is a later revenue and collection bridge for this project. If the company cites the full tier as order visibility, ask whether it is an enforceable minimum, a ceiling, or a classification based on potential usage. Do not count the tier as backlog without a reconciliation. [43]

The older APSSDC notice from January 2026 described L1 selection and said formal contract execution and performance security were still pending. The September 2026 notice provides a later Notification of Award with terms. The two filings may represent a progression or separate scopes; they do not explicitly reconcile the amounts. This is a management-diligence question. The company should disclose whether the later award supersedes or expands the earlier notice, and how much revenue is recognized only after the customer accepts deliverables. [5] [43]

For the attendance products, count active rather than registered users. The Higher Education agreement covers about 1.3 million students, staff and users across 3,900 institutions, while Telangana’s work orders specify about one million users across several education bodies. These are significant populations, but no audited active-user or paid-authentication count is disclosed. Ask for uptime, false-match/false-reject rates, accepted attendance records, contract renewals and support effort. Those metrics connect management’s deployment claims to customer value and cash. [6] [11]

For the next results cycle, you can organize the monitoring dashboard around leading, conversion and lagging indicators. Leading indicators are awards, user scope, scheduled go-live and product development. Conversion indicators are acceptance, active billable sessions, renewal and collection lag. Lagging indicators are revenue, segment margin, CFO, capex and impairment. The latest APSSDC award makes usage minutes and completed interview sessions measurable; the Higher Education SLA makes authentications and renewals measurable. None is currently reported in a way that lets investors calculate cohort economics. [1] [3] [6] [43]

The management walk-the-talk audit has a short horizon. FY2025 communications emphasized SaaS, government relationships and growing AI capability; FY2026 produced audited revenue and profit growth. The September 2026 NIA award is a specific new milestone. At the same time, the high-volume identification claims from the November 2025 presentation are not reconciled to paid active users or collected revenue, and H1 FY2027 cash conversion deteriorated. The promise of foundational platforms remains open until new awards convert into accepted, repeatable and cash-generative deployments. [1] [3] [7] [43]

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION — choose indicators that can falsify the story
book_callouts.text: The best KPI is one that could tell you the thesis is failing. For RNIT, that means acceptance, collections, renewal and delivery effort.
